<a name="rest"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Rest

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Rest
```

Source: [framework/interfaces/Rest.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/interfaces/Rest.php#L25)

Class Rest
Answers HTTP requests with capabilities, in JSON:

- Route::capability('POST', '/books', 'create_book') maps one route to one capability
- Route::capabilities('/capabilities') adds GET /capabilities (what the caller may call, with the input schemas, and the CSRF token of the session in "csrf") and POST /capabilities/{name} (call any capability by name: the JS client of the Vue apps uses it)

Who calls: a personal access token (Authorization: Bearer cq_...), the legacy API key, or the signed-in user. Calls
made with the session cookie need the CSRF token in an X-CSRF-Token header (or \_token) unless they only read.
Inputs: the JSON body (or form fields, or the query string for GET), then the route variables, which win.
Responses: 200 with the result ({"data": ...}), 201 when a POST creates, or {"error": {"code", "message", "fields"}}
with 401, 403, 404, 409 or 422.

<a name="client"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Client

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Client
```

Source: [framework/interfaces/Client.php:19](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/interfaces/Client.php#L19)

Class Client
One ES module, no dependency, for the Vue apps, the Vite SPA and Node scripts: one async function per capability
(create_book becomes createBook) plus call(name, input) and capabilities(). It talks to Route::capabilities().

- In a page of the application it uses the session: the cookie, and the CSRF token it reads once from GET {prefix}. Elsewhere (Node, another origin) configure({ baseUrl, token }) sends a personal access token.
- A refused call throws CapabilityError with status, code (invalid, forbidden...), message and fields.

## class Caligrafy\Mcp\Http

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Mcp;

class Http
```

Source: [framework/interfaces/Mcp/Http.php:22](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/interfaces/Mcp/Http.php#L22)

Class Http
One JSON-RPC message per POST, answered with application/json (no event stream: every tool answers at once).

- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer &lt;personal access token&gt;. Without a valid token: 401 with WWW-Authenticate.
- Origin: a browser request from another site is refused (403), against DNS rebinding. Allowed: no Origin header (agents), the application's own host, and the origins listed in MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma separated).
- Notifications are answered 202 with no body. GET and DELETE answer 405 (no server-initiated stream, no sessions).

<a name="mcp-server"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Mcp\Server

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Mcp;

class Server
```

Source: [framework/interfaces/Mcp/Server.php:26](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/interfaces/Mcp/Server.php#L26)

Class Server
JSON-RPC 2.0 messages of MCP, independent of the transport (Http for Streamable HTTP, caligrafer mcp for stdio):
initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call; notifications get no answer.

The tools are the capabilities the context may call, with their input schema and the hints agents use to decide
when to ask the user first (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint). A tool call goes through Capabilities::call(): the same
permission checks, validation and audit as every other channel. A refused call (invalid input, forbidden...) is a
tool result with isError, so the agent can read the reason and correct itself; protocol errors are JSON-RPC errors.

### Constants

+ `PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = array('2025-11-25', '2025-06-18', '2025-03-26', '2024-11-05')`
+ `PARSE_ERROR = -32700`
+ `INVALID_REQUEST = -32600`
+ `METHOD_NOT_FOUND = -32601`
+ `INVALID_PARAMS = -32602`
+ `INTERNAL_ERROR = -32603`
